brief: Engineering lead: finished 9-month migration from monolith to microservices at a fintech; p99 latency down 40%; 3 teams involved.
original_draft:
After 9 months, 3 teams, and countless whiteboard sessions — we did it.

This week, we officially completed our migration from a monolith to microservices at our fintech.

The results speak for themselves:
📉 p99 latency down 40%
🚀 Deployments that used to take hours now take minutes
🤝 3 teams shipping independently without stepping on each other

But here's what nobody tells you about migrations like this: the technical work is the easy part. The hard part is alignment. Getting 3 teams to agree on service boundaries, ownership, and standards took more energy than any line of code.

My biggest lessons:
1. Start with the domain, not the technology
2. Migrate incrementally — big bangs fail
3. Celebrate small wins along the way

To everyone who says microservices are overhyped: sometimes they're exactly the right tool for the job.

What's the biggest migration you've ever been part of? I'd love to hear your war stories in the comments. 👇

brief: Personal story: laid off from a big tech co in January; 6 months later now leads product at a 30-person startup; 200+ applications sent.
facts: laid off from a big tech co in January
original_draft:
In January, I was laid off from a big tech company.

Today, 6 months later, I'm proud to share that I've joined a 30-person startup to lead product.

The months in between? The hardest of my career.

200+ applications sent. Countless rejections. Interviews that went nowhere. Days where I questioned everything I thought I knew about my own value.

But here's what I learned:
💡 Your job is not your identity
💡 Rejection is redirection
💡 The right opportunity is worth the wait

To anyone navigating a layoff right now: I see you. The process is brutal, and the silence is deafening. But you are not your job title, and this season will not last forever.

To the hiring managers who took the time to send thoughtful rejections — thank you. It mattered more than you know.

New chapter starts now. Let's build. 🚀

If you're job searching and need support, my DMs are always open.

brief: Hot take: most AI agent startups are thin wrappers around the same 3 foundation models; moats are workflow depth and data, not prompts.
facts: moats are workflow depth and data
original_draft:
Hot take: most AI agent startups are thin wrappers around the same 3 foundation models.

There — I said it.

Every week, I see another "revolutionary AI agent" launch. And every week, the pattern is the same: a clever prompt, a polished UI, and a foundation model doing all the heavy lifting underneath.

Here's the uncomfortable truth: prompts are not a moat. Anyone can copy them in an afternoon.

So what actually creates defensibility?
🔑 Workflow depth — embedding so deeply into how a team works that switching becomes painful
🔑 Proprietary data — feedback loops that make your product smarter every single day

The winners in this space won't be the ones with the best demo. They'll be the ones who understand their customers' workflows better than anyone else on the planet.

If you're building an AI agent startup, ask yourself one question: if the model providers shipped your feature tomorrow, what would be left?

Agree or disagree? Let me know in the comments. 👇

brief: Recap of attending SaaStr Annual; 3 takeaways: PLG is maturing, AI pricing is unsettled, community-led growth is back; met 40+ founders.

I met 40+ founders, sat in on dozens of sessions, and had more hallway conversations than I can count. Here are my top 3 takeaways:

1️⃣ PLG is maturing. Product-led growth isn't just a buzzword anymore — companies are getting genuinely sophisticated about layering sales on top of self-serve motions.

The energy in SaaS right now is unlike anything I've seen in years.

brief: Thought piece: why ~70% of enterprise AI pilots never reach production; blames data readiness and missing process redesign, not the models.
facts: ~70% of enterprise AI pilots never reach production
original_draft:
Roughly 70% of enterprise AI pilots never reach production.

Let that sink in.

And here's the part most people get wrong: it's not the models. The models are ready. They've been ready.

The real culprits?

1. Data readiness. Most enterprises are sitting on fragmented, inconsistent, poorly governed data. You can't build production AI on a foundation of spreadsheets and silos.

2. Missing process redesign. Too many companies bolt AI onto existing workflows and expect magic. AI doesn't just automate a process — it demands that you rethink it. Skip that step, and your pilot dies in the demo phase.

The companies succeeding with AI aren't the ones with the best models. They're the ones who did the unglamorous work first: cleaning their data, redesigning their processes, and preparing their people for change.

The technology isn't the bottleneck. We are.

Is your organization struggling to move AI from pilot to production? What's actually holding you back? Share your experience below. 👇

brief: Product launch: v2 of analytics tool "Clearlens" adds session replay and funnel comparison; built from 300+ customer interviews; 14 beta customers.

Today's the day. Clearlens v2 is officially live! 🎉

Over the past year, we conducted 300+ customer interviews. We listened, we learned, and we built.

The two most requested features are finally here:

🎬 Session Replay — watch exactly how users experience your product, moment by moment
📊 Funnel Comparison — compare conversion funnels side by side to see what's actually moving the needle

A massive thank you to our 14 beta customers who tested, broke, and helped us refine these features over the past few months. Your feedback shaped every pixel.

Building this release taught us one thing above all: your customers already know what your roadmap should be. You just have to ask them.

This is our biggest release yet — and honestly, we're just getting started.

Curious what your users are really doing inside your product? Come see for yourself. Link in the comments.

What should we build next? Let us know below. 👇
